comparison: Both address the foundational immobilization model (C1, C2, C5, C6). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging experimental data showing dose-response and temporal dissociation. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one fundamentally challenging the model as producing stress/gain-of-function rather than passive loss, while another acknowledges thorough examination but notes incomplete cold exposure analysis.

Both evaluate baseline characterization claims (C72-C75). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as establishing temporal dissociation between cold intolerance and muscle atrophy. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, questioning whether locomotor activity measurements account for the work of dragging casts and whether heat demand is comparable when mice are wrapped in gypsum.

Partial overlap on muscle thermogenic capacity (C3, C4). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED evidence for suppressed muscle thermogenesis through gene expression and metabolomics. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the immobilization model itself, with one arguing results reflect stress rather than thermogenic challenge.

Both address muscle thermogenic capacity and broader conclusions (C76-C78, C79, C81). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for impaired muscle thermogenesis, though notes generalization to all mammals is overstated. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, attributing findings to stress and depleted calorie reserves rather than organ communication during thermogenic challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C7-C11, C62, C80) on BAT compensatory activation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through denervation experiments establishing sympathetic dependence. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one rejecting the interpretation as BAT being 'stressed' and 'super-induced but relatively poor functioning,' while another finds the organ interaction convincingly demonstrated.

Perfect claim overlap (C12-C18) on systemic metabolic responses. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED evidence through metabolomics, gene expression, and denervation experiments. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one interpreting changes as cachectic effects from stress and lipid reserve depletion, and the editor noting incomplete evidence due to unaccounted energetic costs.

Perfect claim overlap (C19-C28, C82) on amino acid redistribution. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive evidence but notes radiotracer limitation. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one viewing findings as stress-induced catabolism and the editor requesting further experiments to directly assess adipose-derived BCAAs in thermogenesis.

Perfect claim overlap (C29-C34) on IL-6 induction. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through denervation and temporal profiling, though muscle IL-6 mechanism unclear. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one viewing IL-6 as part of stress/cachectic response, while another acknowledges IL-6 is likely involved in amino acid supply mechanism.

Perfect claim overlap (C35-C44) on IL-6 KO phenotyping. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through comprehensive characterization with multiple independent measurements. Peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging the genetic loss-of-function approach provides stronger evidence, though overall interpretation remains contested due to immobilization model concerns.

Partial overlap (C45, C46) on IL-6 rescue experiments. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for establishing IL-6 sufficiency, though mechanism unclear. Peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED, with one noting the experiments convincingly demonstrate organ interaction significance, and these gain-of-function experiments not directly criticized.

High overlap (C48-C53) on tissue-specific IL-6 functions via iBAT removal. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for demonstrating distinct endocrine and autocrine/paracrine functions, though inference is indirect. Peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging these tissue-specific manipulations help address mechanistic questions and are not directly criticized.

Perfect claim overlap (C54-C60) on generalization to other physiological conditions. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, strengthening physiological relevance through cold exposure and stress paradigms. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with fundamental critique of immobilization as stress paradigm applying, though cold exposure experiments may be less confounded and one reviewer notes this area needs more thorough analysis.

OpenEval evaluates integrative summary claims (C61, C63, C64, C89) as SUPPORTED by collective evidence, noting need for more sophisticated tracing experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific summary claims.
OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C65-C71) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates contextual literature claims (C84-C88) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.

Both address interpretive conclusions (C79, C81) about muscle thermogenic capacity limitations. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes generalization to all mammals is overstated. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one disputing conclusions as attributable to stress/depleted reserves and the editor noting evidence is incomplete.
